"""Appendix Fig A4 (C3): dependence of the Chin regression on the treated share p at every degree.
Top row: bias; bottom row: SD (dashed) and RMSE (solid) -- one column per target degree d in {5, 20, 80}, one colour per mechanism:
(a) linear fraction, (c) saturating, and the exploratory (g) convex mirror (open markers, labelled * = exploratory; only the p values the run grid carries).
Bars are the Monte Carlo 95% intervals of `claims/c3_p_dependence.csv`. core cells, s = 1/2, sigma = 0.5, Bernoulli design.
The DM bias (about -0.5 at every p) is outside the plotted range of the top row and is not drawn.
Usage: figA4_p.py RESULTS_DIR OUT_DIR
"""
import argparse
import pathlib

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

import common
import style

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("data"); ap.add_argument("out")
a = ap.parse_args()
style.apply()
_, meta = common.load(a.data, "cells")
d = pd.read_csv(pathlib.Path(a.data) / "claims" / "c3_p_dependence.csv")
d = d[d.estimator == "chin"]
MEC = [("a", "(a) linear", "#0072B2", "o", True), ("c", "(c) saturating", "#009E73", "D", True), ("g", "(g) convex*", "#CC79A7", "^", False)]
fig, axs = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(style.TEXTWIDTH, 3.2), sharex=True, sharey="row", gridspec_kw=dict(wspace=0.08, hspace=0.12))
for j, dd in enumerate([5, 20, 80]):
    for m, lab, col, mk, filled in MEC:
        t = d[(d.mechanism == m) & (d.d_target == dd)].sort_values("p")
        if not len(t):
            continue
        mfc = col if filled else "white"
        axs[0, j].errorbar(t.p, t.bias, yerr=[t.bias - t.bias_mc_lo, t.bias_mc_hi - t.bias], color=col, marker=mk, mfc=mfc, ms=3.6, lw=1.0, capsize=1.5, elinewidth=0.7, label=lab)
        axs[1, j].errorbar(t.p, t.rmse, yerr=[t.rmse - t.rmse_mc_lo, t.rmse_mc_hi - t.rmse], color=col, marker=mk, mfc=mfc, ms=3.6, lw=1.0, capsize=1.5, elinewidth=0.7)
        axs[1, j].plot(t.p, t.sd, color=col, marker=mk, mfc=mfc, ms=2.6, lw=0.9, ls="--")
    axs[0, j].axhline(0, color="k", lw=0.6)
    axs[0, j].set_title(f"$d={dd}$", fontsize=style.MIN_PT, pad=3)
    axs[1, j].set_xlabel("treated share $p$"); axs[1, j].set_xticks([0.1, 0.5, 0.9]); axs[1, j].set_yscale("log")
axs[0, 0].set_ylabel("bias"); axs[1, 0].set_ylabel("RMSE, SD")
axs[1, 0].set_yticks([0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1]); axs[1, 0].set_yticklabels(["0.03", "0.1", "0.3", "1"]); axs[1, 0].minorticks_off()
for ax in axs[0, 1:]:
    ax.tick_params(labelleft=False)
h, l = axs[0, 0].get_legend_handles_labels()
for ax in axs[0]:
    hh, ll = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
    for x, y in zip(hh, ll):

from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

fig.legend(h, l, frameon=False, loc="lower center", ncol=5, bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.12), columnspacing=0.9, handletextpad=0.4)

    df = pd.read_parquet(d / f"{name}.parquet") if (d / f"{name}.parquet").exists() else pd.read_csv(d / f"{name}.csv")
    if "estimator" in df:
        df["estimator"] = df["estimator"].replace(EST_NAME)
    if "design" in df:
        df["design"] = df["design"].replace(DESIGN_NAME)
    if "d_target" in df and "mean_degree" not in df:
        df["mean_degree"] = df["d_target"]
    meta_path = d / f"{name}.meta.json"
    meta = json.loads(meta_path.read_text()) if meta_path.exists() else {"fixture": True}
    return df, meta


CORE_RUN = r"core_SBM_n3000_d\d+_p[\d.]+$"   # run ids of the core family (SBM, n~3000, Bernoulli, iid baseline, true graph)


def core(df, **kw):
    """Rows of the core family (run_id `core_SBM_n3000_d*_p*`) matching kw (columns compared exactly, floats with isclose)."""
    import numpy as np
    m = df["run_id"].astype(str).str.match(CORE_RUN).to_numpy().copy()
    for k, v in kw.items():
        m &= np.isclose(df[k], v) if isinstance(v, float) else (df[k] == v).to_numpy()
    return df[m]


def out_dir(meta, root):
    """Delivered outputs go to <root> only for real analysis results; a layout fixture never does."""
    if meta.get("fixture", False):
        p = pathlib.Path("/tmp/figtab_layout")
        print("FIXTURE data: writing layout check to", p, file=sys.stderr)
    else:
        p = pathlib.Path(root)
    p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return p


def coverage_population(cells, sigma=0.5):
    """The cells behind every coverage number of the paper (Fig 9, Table A3): Chin regression, Bernoulli designs, mechanisms (a)-(f),
    the true graph (no edge-noise, no-baseline sanity or convex-mirror runs), one `sigma`, HC0 coverage on all assignment draws."""
    import numpy as np
    k = cells[(cells.estimator == "Chin") & np.isclose(cells.sigma, sigma) & cells.coverage_hc.notna() & cells.mechanism.isin(list("abcdef"))]
    k = k[(k.edge_noise_q == 0) & ~k.run_id.str.match(r"(sanity|convex|pfine)_")]
    return k[k.design == "bernoulli"].copy()

        ax.axhline(r.rmse_or_fit, color="#0072B2", ls="--", lw=1.2, label="parameter fitted (profiled)")
        ax.axhline(r.rmse_dm, color="k", ls=":", lw=1.2, label="DM")
        ax.set_yscale("log")

shown.message:
I added one new appendix figure on the fitted-form oracle. Two items are still waiting on analysis, so `figtab-repo`#2 stays open. I checked the figure by eye and by a PDF scan (smallest text 8.0 pt). I haven't seen it in a system build.

- **New figure A9** (`figures/figA9_orfit.pdf`, `figA9_orfit.csv`, 393 × 281 pt) shows why the fitted-form oracle (`or_fit`) is worse than difference in means (DM) at d ≥ 20. It draws, from `results/or_fit_check.csv`:
  - RMSE of the oracle with the shape parameter held at each grid value, for (c) and (e) at d = 5, 20, 80;
  - the known-parameter oracle, the fitted one and DM on the same axes;
  - the share of draws whose fit lands at a grid end, in each panel title: 5% / 59% / 86% for (c) and 58% / 82% / 86% for (e) at d = 5 / 20 / 80.
- **Delivery:** the generator is pushed to `paper-repo` `dev` and to `figtab-repo` `main`. The caption draft and facts are in `figures/CAPTIONS.md`, and `REPRODUCE.md` lists the new generator and input. I told the report role on `figtab-repo`#3 (comment 148) that the figure is optional for the nine pages, since it sits in the appendix.
- **One surprise in the numbers:** for (c) at d = 20 the RMSE is flat (0.215–0.217) for κ from 0.5 to 2 and is 0.233 at the true value 3. I stated only that in the caption and gave no explanation for it.
- **Waiting on analysis:**
  - the held-out constant's absolute R² of log|bias|, for Table 2's reference block;
  - the P6 interval table, for the Fig 9 coverage-vs-width panel.

Both are asked for on `experiment-repo`#9, which analysis closed without them.
